steps.text: A high-severity event consistency problem. The order placed event is sent inside the database transaction, before it commits, so if the commit fails other services hear about an order that was never saved. Broker errors are lost too, since nothing waits for the send. Use a transactional outbox: save the event in the same transaction, and publish after the commit.

A medium-severity layering issue. This handler lives in the application layer, but it uses the TypeORM data source and entity directly. That ties the use case to the database library and makes it harder to test. Depend on an order repository interface from the domain instead, and implement it in infrastructure.

A low-severity point about the event itself. The payload is an inline object with a plain string topic. Other services depend on this shape, so it deserves a shared, versioned contract. Adding an event ID and a timestamp would also help consumers handle duplicates.
